test_name: PE import identity survives read-only propagation
speed_method: Interleaved whole-binary decompile-all --json --no-vars on crypto4.exe, exact rebased pre-fix versus fixed release binaries, one warmup and median of 5
decisions: The filed hypothesis is upheld: ActionVarnodeProps observed an RX PE IAT slot as both readonly and externref, then fillin_read_only replaced the slot with its on-disk hint/name RVA before ActionDeindirect could consume the external-reference identity.

The fix snapshots Varnode::is_external_ref and excludes that Varnode from the entire readonly-fold branch. This is the narrow semantic invariant: loader-resolved identity outranks file-byte propagation under readonly, dynrelocs and litpoolconst alike.

Subtracting PE IAT ranges from executable literal-pool ranges was rejected. It would special-case one producer, duplicate the stronger externref fact, and leave program-wide readonly able to repeat the same corruption.
The existing option boundaries are preserved. peimportcall off does not paint externref and therefore retains the raw-call rendering; no PE import ranges, defaults, or command semantics changed.

The acceptance was strengthened during reduction: it requires two distinct GetDlgItemTextA calls with all four arguments and excludes both the original witness RVA 0x173dc and the fixture RVA 0x10c4, so deleting a call or cosmetically replacing one target cannot pass.

acceptance.result: pass 3/3; transition closed; all five clauses passed
acceptance.unpatched_result: fails both required call matches and emits the raw 0x10c4 call target

fixture.shape: PE32 i386; code, IAT and import metadata share one allocated executable read-only section
fixture.determinism: generator output compared byte-for-byte with the committed fixture

tests.console: verify_pe_import_readonly.rs: peimportcall off remains raw; default and explicit on retain the exact nested VirtualAlloc/GetModuleHandleA call; peimportcall on plus readonly on remains named
tests.cli: tests/cli/pe-import-calls-become.json; make test-cli 133/133 after the final rebase
tests.stage_test_rationale: The premise is loader-created PE externref metadata and section permissions, which the raw XML stage corpus cannot express; the object-loader console test is the two-arm integration gate.

regression_sweep.method: Compared pre-fix and fixed release builds with kuna decompile-all --json --no-vars on the real crypto4.exe witness, then repeated the comparison on the ordinary writable-IAT pe_imports.exe control.
regression_sweep.control: pe_imports.exe: 150 functions, byte-identical full JSON before/after
regression_sweep.original_selector: crypto4.exe 0x40341c contains both GetDlgItemTextA calls and no 0x173dc

known_risk.finding: crypto4.exe sub_4039b2 still truncates after GlobalLock because an imported-call no-return attribute is misassociated; later imports are omitted.
known_risk.classification: pre-existing peimportcall/no-return defect exposed by restoring import identity, not caused by the externref guard
known_risk.evidence: The exact truncation is already present on unpatched main with option litpoolconst off, and fixed-default output is byte-identical to that pre-fix workaround for this function.
known_risk.disposition: Recorded for follow-up; deliberately not expanded into a second semantic fix in this small P3 change.

speed.method: Interleaved exact pre-fix/fixed release binaries on the 93-function crypto4.exe witness; both arms used the same rebased source and runtime specs.
speed.note: The small negative delta is treated as timing noise, not as evidence of a speedup. The evidence supports only that no regression above the 5% budget was observed; acceptance wall-clock samples are not used as performance evidence.
